title: saffron-inference-cost-journey-calc-and-recs
content:
Context and high-level objective:

This is a working calculation and recommendation set for Saffron Health (pilot account). Goal: quantify expected monthly cost delta after applying a package of Redwood Optimize recommendations, show per-recommendation impact, call out open engineering/ops questions, and provide a migration playbook (minimal disruption).

Source data (customer-provided + telemetry):
- Monthly active API keys: 3 (prod, staging, test) but >95% traffic through prod key.
- Observed monthly tokens (generation + prompt): 1,420,000,000 tokens (1.42B).
- Primary workload split: 62% chat (long-context generation), 28% embeddings, 10% classification/rerank.
- Current model variants: prod uses model-A-32b-fp16 (baseline), embeddings on embed-large, some reroute to embed-small for cheap tenants but Saffron pinned to embed-large.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 450ms, some tail spikes to ~1.2s during peak.
- Current billed monthly spend (baseline telemetry + invoices): $57,600 (rounded).

Assumptions used in these calculations (explicit):
1) Baseline per-token cost inferred from invoices: $57,600 / 1.42B = ~$0.0000406 per token. We will keep per-token baseline figure fixed for sensitivity rows.
2) Embeddings and chat accounted proportionally to token counts (chat consumes more tokens per request).
3) KV/prefix cache effective reduction applies only to chat workload and only to repeat/prefix tokens (we assume 28% of chat tokens are cacheable for Saffron based on traffic analysis).
4) Quantization and 8-bit/4-bit model variants reduce per-token compute cost; we model these as multiplicative factors on per-token cost for the model-family portion of traffic.
5) Batching improvements change effective compute utilization and therefore reduce unit cost by amortizing overhead; we apply as a percentage multiplier to the remaining compute cost post-quantization/cache.
6) Model swap to a smaller but Redwood-verified variant is applied to 35% of chat requests (non-guardrail-critical paths).
7) Latency budget preserved: any recommendation must keep p95 < 500ms for 90% of requests; fallback policy used for rare long-tail cases.

Baseline breakdown (approx):
- Total tokens: 1,420,000,000
- Baseline spend: $57,600
- Effective baseline unit cost: $0.00004056 / token
- Workload token split (approx):
  - Chat: 62% -> 880.4M tokens
  - Embeddings: 28% -> 397.6M tokens
  - Rerank/classification: 10% -> 142.0M tokens

Recommendation bundle (Redwood Optimize quick-win pack):
1) KV/prefix caching (enable persistent conversation prefix cache + client-side hints): expected cache hit 28% of chat tokens -> reduces chat token billable by that percentage for hits.
2) Quantization profile: move model-A-32b-fp16 -> model-A-32b-q4 (4-bit) for non-critical routes. Estimated compute cost reduction 45% on quantized portion.
3) Smart batching: enable request coalescing during 50ms window + increase batch size for steady-state -> estimated 18% lower effective compute unit cost after quantization.
4) Model routing: route 35% of chat requests to model-B-7b-8k (verified for Saffron prompt templates) -> reduces per-token cost on routed traffic by ~70% compared to baseline.
5) Embedding tiering: route 30% of low-value embedding calls to embed-small and keep 70% on embed-large -> ~40% saving on that fraction of embedding spend.
6) Autoscale tuning + reserved pool for peak windows: minor effect on unit cost but reduces tail p95 spikes; modeled as 0% change to spend here but decreases risk.

Step-by-step arithmetic (rounded figures):
1) Chat tokens: 880.4M. Apply KV cache hit reduction: 28% of chat tokens are served from cache -> cached tokens = 246.5M (not billed) -> billable chat tokens after cache = 633.9M.
2) Of billable chat tokens, route 35% to 7b model: routed tokens = 222.9M, remaining chat on quantized baseline = 411.0M.
3) Unit cost multipliers (relative to baseline unit cost $0.00004056):
   - Baseline (32b fp16): 1.00x
   - Quantized 32b q4: 0.55x (45% cheaper)
   - 7b-8k variant: 0.30x (70% cheaper)
   - Embedding small: 0.60x of embed-large unit cost (40% cheaper)

Breakdown compute: (using baseline unit cost for all token math then applying multipliers)
- Chat routed -> 222.9M tokens * $0.00004056 * 0.30 = $2,713 (rounded)
- Chat quantized -> 411.0M tokens * $0.00004056 * 0.55 = $9,173
- Cached chat -> 246.5M tokens * $0.00004056 * 0.00 = $0 (assume no billing for cache hits)
=> Total chat after recs = $11,886 (vs baseline chat cost baseline_chat_cost = 880.4M * $0.00004056 = $35,730)

Embeddings:
- Total embedding tokens 397.6M. Split 70% embed-large (278.3M), 30% embed-small (119.3M).
- Baseline embedding cost portion (from baseline unit cost) = 397.6M * $0.00004056 = $16,126
- After recs: embed-large portion cost = 278.3M * $0.00004056 * 1.00 = $11,289
             embed-small portion cost = 119.3M * $0.00004056 * 0.60 = $2,903
=> Total embeddings after recs = $14,192 (vs baseline $16,126)

Rerank/classification (142.0M tokens):
- Conservative approach: keep on baseline model but enable batching -> apply batching multiplier -18% effective cost reduction -> 142.0M * $0.00004056 * 0.82 = $4,727 (baseline rerank cost = 142.0M * $0.00004056 = $5,759)

Subtotal after core recs (before applying additional batching uplift across chat quantized portion):
- Chat: $11,886
- Embeddings: $14,192
- Rerank: $4,727
=> Subtotal = $30,805

Batching second-order effect: we modeled quantized chat & rerank with 18% lower costs where applicable already for rerank; for chat quantized branch we included quantization but not batching above. Apply an additional 18% improvement on quantized chat portion ($9,173 -> *0.82 = $7,519). Adjustments: subtract old quantized chat $9,173 and replace with $7,519 -> delta -$1,654. New chat total = routed $2,713 + quantized+batches $7,519 + cached $0 = $10,232. New subtotal = $10,232 + $14,192 + $4,727 = $29,151

Other small adders: monitoring/export costs, extra inference orchestration, estimated +$500/month (ops).

Final estimate after Redwood Optimize quick-win pack:
- Estimated monthly spend: $29,651 ($29,151 + $500 ops buffer)
- Baseline: $57,600
- Absolute savings: $27,949 / month
- Percent savings: 48.5% (~49%)

Sensitivity analysis (quick):
- If cache hit rate is only 18% (vs 28% assumed) -> chat cached tokens = 158.5M; recompute quickly reduces total savings by ~6pp (savings ~42%).
- If quantization only yields 30% reduction (vs 45%) -> savings drop ~8pp.
- If routing to 7b must be limited to 15% of chat (not 35%) -> routing benefit drops, total savings ~38%.

Risk & migration notes:
- Quality regression risk: model-B-7b must be validated on Saffron's 20 canonical prompts and 40 edge cases (see linked Confluence tests). If mismatch found, decrease routing fraction or increase guardrails.
- Latency risk: enabling batching can increase p95 for very small requests; mitigate by maintaining a low-latency fast-path and a short batching window (<=50ms).
- Cache invalidation: conversation semantics must be validated to ensure cached prefixes are safe; ops needs a safelist for prompts with PII or ephemeral tokens.

Open engineering/ops questions (short list):
- Can runtime enforce per-route quantization variant toggles without requiring model restart? (ticket filed: JIRA-9123)
- What SLO change (if any) is acceptable for 5% of requests during batching window? Who signs off?
- Can we expose cache hit telemetry at the token-level back to customer for validation (preferably via internal metrics or audit endpoints)?

Playbook (high level) for rollout (2-week phased pilot):
Week 0: prechecks & smoke tests - Validate model-B-7b on canonical prompt set; run A/B on staging traffic (1% of prod).
Week 1: staged traffic rollouts - 10% chat -> model-B, enable prefix cache for 10% of users, monitor quality and p95.
Week 2: expand to 35% routing if quality ok; enable quantization on remaining routes; enable batching with conservative window.
Post-rollout: monitor cost dashboards, tune cache hit percentages, and prepare a 30-day retrospective.

Deliverables for customer success / account team:
- One-pager showing before/after monthly invoice projection (this doc + simplified numbers).
- A shared spreadsheet with per-tab scenarios (best / expected / worse) + comfort ranges. Linked artifact: (sheet id: GDRIVE-XXXXXX in Confluence page).
- Runbook for rollback (steps to turn off routing, disable quantized model, and purge caches).

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: finalize canonical prompt suite and upload to Confluence (due 2025-03-18).
- Marco: spin up a staging A/B job and capture 7-day quality metrics (JIRA-9140).
- Leah: prepare the customer-facing one-pager and updated cost dashboard in Console (task 2025-03-20).
- Eng (SRE/Runtime): answer the runtime quantization toggle question and ETA for token-level cache telemetry (blocker: JIRA-9123).

Appendix: quick numbers summary (rounded)
- Baseline monthly: $57.6k
- After recs (expected): $29.7k
- Savings: ~$28k / month (~49%)
- Key levers: cache (28% chat token elimination), model routing (35% chat -> 7b), quantization (45% reduction on quantized compute), batching (18% secondary reduction)

Notes/loose items to capture in spreadsheet: exact per-model unit costs, tokenization differences between models, embedding vs generation unit cost normalization, reserved pool amortization if customer wants a dedicated commit (changes ROI calculations).

-- End of working calc doc --

(Do not publish to customer until: canonical prompt validation complete, runtime quantization toggle signed off, and a 7-day staging A/B shows quality delta <= 2% on NPS/accuracy proxies.)
